summary: M3-S04 tested. All 3 runnable acceptance tests passed: both always-on structural checks (xml 3/3 parse; manifest 2/2 types <-> files, two-way consistent, no wildcards, deploy-order.md and owner-writer-map.md correctly excluded as non-metadata) and the one declared checker (check_case_management_setup.py, build scope) at exit 0, paired with check-outputs ok (4/4 declared outputs present, non-empty, parsing). 2 manual tests deferred to the M3 gate, neither ticked here. Step set to tested. Recorded verbatim per instruction, not resolved: the step's title and the first manual test (W02) assert routing on Case.Origin AND the Account support tier, but the built assignment-rule artefact routes on Case.Origin only -- deploy-order.md section 6 row 1 documents this as a deliberate omission (no answer names a tier->queue mapping and no skill grounds a cross-object criteriaItems notation on a Case rule), so the mismatch is a plan/artefact disagreement for the M3 gate to adjudicate, not a test failure here.
confidence_rationale: Step 7 rubric, HIGH row: every declared test ran (checker, xml, manifest) or was correctly classified as manual (2), both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed. No MEDIUM trigger fired -- no command test was refused, no manifest exclusion was needed for a coverage-gap type (both AssignmentRules and AutoResponseRules are ordinary standalone-file types), and check-outputs reported no missing, empty or malformed declared output. No LOW trigger fired -- the one declared checker resolved to exactly one existing script, the artefact directory holds 5 files (2 XML + package.xml + 2 markdown), and every exit code was captured to tests/M3-S04/. The title/manual-test vs artefact mismatch is a build-content ambiguity for the human gate, not a defect in this agent's own test execution, so it does not lower confidence under this step's own rubric.

process_observations.observation: Rule-entry order inside Case_Intake_Routing is load-bearing and correct: the Email-Billing entry (Billing queue) precedes the Email-Support entry (Tier_1_General), and a criteria-less catch-all (also Tier_1_General) is last with no booleanFilter -- matching skills/admin/assignment-rules SKILL.md 'Active Rule Limit and Rule Entry Order' (first match wins, evaluation stops). Exactly one assignmentRule carries <active>true</active>, which check_case_management_setup.py's declared test independently confirms.

The auto-response rule's senderEmail and replyToEmail both read support-noreply@acme.example, matching the binding operator note on plan.json steps[M3-S04].notes (2026-09-12T05:12:42Z) and avoiding both of this org's live Email-to-Case routing addresses (support@/billing@ per M3-S03 settings) -- the mail-loop condition admin/assignment-rules gotcha 6 and admin/email-to-case-configuration gotcha 3 both warn against is not present in the built artefact.

check_assignment_rules.py is undeclared on this step (informational, per plan.json steps[M3-S04].inputs.note) and was run anyway as an observation, not a test. Its exit code and message reproduce deploy-order.md section 7's prediction exactly at both scopes: exit 1 on "target 'Tier_1_General' appears in multiple rule entries" at step and build scope alike, with the step-scope run additionally emitting AR-LOOP-02 (no routing-address inventory in scope) that the build-scope run does not. The duplication is deliberate by construction (Q18 support@ -> Tier 1, Q26 catch-all -> Tier 1), so this non-passing exit code was correctly left undeclared rather than forced into acceptance_tests[].

Recorded verbatim, not resolved, per this run's instructions: steps[M3-S04].title reads 'Case assignment rules and auto-response rules driven by Origin and account support tier', and the first manual acceptance test (W02) asserts the active rule's entries 'route on Case.Origin and the Account support tier only'. The built assignmentRules file routes on Case.Origin only -- no criteriaItems anywhere in the file names Account.Support_Tier__c or any related-object field. deploy-order.md section 6 row 1 (written by metadata-builder) records this as deliberate: Q25 names Support_Tier__c as available at save but no answer maps a tier to a queue, and no skill under skills/ grounds a related-object criteriaItems/field notation on a Case assignment rule, so writing one would have been a guessed value shape. The mismatch is between the plan's own title/test text and what the plan's own answers can ground -- this agent does not adjudicate it.

deploy-order.md is produced on this run (per metadata-builder's own contract) but is not in steps[M3-S04].outputs[], so check-outputs never adjudicates it -- the fourth consecutive M3 step where this pattern appears (decisions.md O-M3S02-03). Not a test failure: check-outputs still returned ok:true for the four outputs that are declared.
M3-S04 is tested; three findings (the title/test mismatch, the undeclared deploy-order.md, and D-M3S02-04's still-open sender-address question) need to reach decisions.md and the workbook.
process_observations.followup_reason: It owns decisions.md, the workbook and traceability.md, and is the next stage once a step reaches tested.

process_observations.observation: The title/manual-test vs artefact mismatch on the Account support tier is exactly the kind of open design question the M3 milestone gate needs adjudicated before acceptance.
process_observations.followup_reason: It compiles the M3 acceptance report and is where a human sees this ambiguity alongside every other M3 step's manual tests.
